We need to read the problem carefully: The function name and description mention "lexicographicallySmallestArray", but the problem statement asks for lexicographically largest array. This is confusing: maybe they want smallest? Actually the given examples produce something like sorted descending within groups.

Let's think: The operation: we can swap any two elements if their absolute difference is <= limit. This is basically we can rearrange elements within each connected component of a graph where edges are defined by difference <= limit. However, we can also do repeated swaps: So the equivalence relation is: we have two elements that can be swapped via a sequence of allowed swaps (i.e., you can swap i and j if there's a path where each adjacent pair satisfies difference <= limit). Equivalent to: The elements are grouped by transitive closure of relation difference <= limit. That is: sort the numbers, then group them where consecutive numbers difference > limit forms a new group. Because if we sort numbers, the relation difference <= limit connects any numbers within the same "interval chain" where each consecutive diff <= limit. Actually relation: we say a and b are "linked" if |a-b| <= limit. This relation is not transitive: e.g., a=1, b=3, limit=2 => |1-3|<=2 true. b=3, c=5 => |3-5|<=2 true. So we have a path linking a and c via b even if |a-c|=4 > limit (still allowed through intermediate). So we can get connectivity in sorted order by considering that any numbers can be swapped if they belong to the same connected component of the graph where edges connect numbers with difference <= limit. For sorted values, connectivity will be groups where each adjacent difference <= limit (the "chain" condition). Indeed, if sorted array a[0]<=a[1]<=...<=a[n-1], then there is an edge between i and i+1 iff a[i+1]-a[i] <= limit. The transitive closure yields that any two elements in the same contiguous segment where all adjacent differences <= limit are connected (since you can go stepwise). Conversely, if there is a gap > limit between a[i] and a[i+1], then no element left of i can be swapped with any element right of i+1 because any path would need to cross that gap, and the edge across the gap would require difference <= limit which fails. So components are contiguous segments in sorted order
